title: What Role Does Denuclearization Have in North Korea-US Dialogue Today?
author: Jessica Earl
text:
In this Feb. 27, 2019, file photo, then-U.S. President Donald Trump shakes hands with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un at the Sofitel Legend Metropole hotel in Hanoi, Vietnam, for their second summit meeting.
Credit: Official White House Photo
With his surprise decision to scale back the recent Ulchi Freedom Shield military exercise on the Korean Peninsula, U.S. President Donald Trump clearly signaled his intent to rekindle dialogue with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. However, rather than receiving praise for the goodwill measure, the effort drew rebuke from the North Korean government, which reiterated its position that it has no interest in renewing engagement as long as the United States holds onto denuclearization as a policy objective.This exchange has renewed debates over long-standing denuclearization policies, particularly as Trump continues his overtures toward the Kim regime in hopes of a possible meeting on the sidelines of the APEC summit in November. Some have argued it is time to abandon denuclearization as a policy goal and shift to arms control, while others contend that such a concession would undermine the global nonproliferation regime and place further stress on allied relationships.[...]
